questions.stem_markdown: Find the quotient and remainder when $x^4 - 3x^3 + 9x^2 - 12x + 27$ is divided by $x^2 + 5$. [3]

mark_scheme_items.content_markdown: Commence division and reach partial quotient of the form $$x^2 \pm 3x$$ or $$x^4 - 3x^3 + 9x^2 - 12x + 27 = (x^2 + 5)(Ax^2 + Bx + C) + Dx + E$$ or $$Ax^4 + Bx^3 + (5A + C)x^2 + 5Bx + 5C$$ and reach $$A = 1$$ and $$B = \pm 3$$

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: $$A = 1, B = -3$$ $$[5A + C = 9 \text{ so } C = 4; 5B + D = -12 \text{ so } D = 3; 5C + E = 27 \text{ so } E = 7]$$. A pair of incorrect statements ‘remainder $$x^2 - 3x + 4$$’ and ‘quotient $$3x + 7$$’ score **M1 A1 A0**.

questions.stem_markdown:
The variables $y$ and $\theta$ satisfy the differential equation

$$(1+y)(1+\cos 2\theta)\frac{dy}{d\theta}=e^{3y}.$$

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: $$\int (1+y)e^{-3y} dy = \int \frac{1}{1+\cos 2\theta} d\theta.$$ Allow $$1/e^{3y}$$ and missing integral signs.
Allow unless clear evidence that formula used has a + sign.

mark_scheme_items.guidance_markdown: $$\frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{9} + C \left( C = \frac{17}{18} \right)$$ Allow $$\alpha y e^{3y}$$ and $$\beta e^{3y}$$. Must have integrated LHS twice.
Or exact equivalent. Exact ISW. Allow $$\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{17}{9} - \frac{14}{9}e^{-3}\right)$$. If $$x$$ instead of $$\theta$$ then withhold final **A1**.
